_comment: Canonical accessible foreground/background token pairings for BDS. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH consumed by: scripts/validate-themes.js (the CI contrast gate), stories/ContrastCompliance.stories.tsx (the Storybook dashboard), and the published foundation doc primitives/color-pairings.mdx (its matrix is generated via `node scripts/validate-themes.js --emit-matrix`). Each pairing is evaluated in BOTH the Brik light and dark default themes. thresholdType assignment follows the locked policy below. A pairing with `darkException` whose DARK result falls below threshold is REPORTED (not failed) and linked to its tracking issue — the known systemic dark-mode service-tier gap. Add a pairing here; never hardcode a pair list in a consumer.
policy: AAA (7:1) for primary body/small text where the surface affords it; AA (4.5:1) for colored brand/service text and on-color neutrals; AA-large (3:1) for large/heading and intentionally-muted/decorative text. Brand-primary fills (CTA buttons/surfaces) and brand accent text hold the vibrant poppy-light brand color (brand-kit canon) and are gated AA-large (3:1) — UI-component fills + large/bold CTA labels and heading/accent text. Text ON the brand fill is ALWAYS white (--bds-text-on-color-dark) at normal weight, ALL sizes incl. body copy (owner-accepted debt at 3.78:1, ADR-015 + its 2026-09-12 amendment); darkening on-color text to --bds-text-primary or bolding body copy to reach large-text are BOTH DISALLOWED on the brand fill. (Distinct rule: --bds-text-brand-primary — Poppy-COLORED text on a neutral surface — still never sizes to small body copy, use --bds-text-primary there; enforced by lint-brand-text, #1064.) Service text-bearing regions use the pale `-lightest` surface step (AAA in light); the mid-tone base step is decorative and gated at AA only.

pairings.note: Button --secondary and Chip --secondary labels. Absent from this dataset until #1689, which is why dark --bds-background-secondary could sit at 3.43:1 against --bds-text-primary unnoticed while the two --bds-text-on-color-light pairings above kept it looking gated. Gated AA-large (3:1), not AA: the token carries two OPPOSITE foregrounds — this light one and the black --bds-text-on-color-light — and no grayscale step clears 4.5:1 for both (-light: 3.43 / 5.46; -dark: 6.16 / 3.04). Both consumers are control labels, the case ADR-015 and #1571 already hold at AA-large. Body copy must NOT use this fill (#1689).

pairings.label: SegmentedControl inactive hover label on tertiary fill
Disabled control label on disabled fill
pairings.note: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components, so this pairing is gated at AA-large (3:1) as intentionally-muted text rather than AA — the point is legibility, not conformance. It is in the dataset because the Figma source emitted fg and bg as the same --bds-color-grayscale-500, painting a disabled Button's label in its own background at 1.00:1 (#1571). A 1:1 pairing can never pass this gate again.

pairings.label: Solid neutral indicator / Solid Tag label on fill
pairings.note: Badge `appearance="solid"`, Dot, Counter and the default Tag (`appearance="solid"`, #2852) render the `neutral` tone on --bds-background-neutral (#1957) — an indicator is a small element placed ON a surface, so its fill is a background token, never a surface one. The label MUST be --bds-text-on-color-dark: --bds-text-neutral resolves to the same --bds-color-system-neutral as the fill and measures 1.00:1, which is exactly the trap the row above records.

pairings.label: Solid info indicator label on fill
pairings.note: Badge `appearance="solid"` and Counter both render the `progress` tone as white-on-fill (Badge.css:133, Counter.css:31) — two shipped consumers, one measurable token pair, the same shape as the two neutral indicator rows above. Was 3.87:1 (AA-large only) and fixed to 6.10:1 by the same #1972 primitive change. This row could not be measured at all before #1965: a comment above --bds-background-info parsed as a declaration and swallowed it, so validate-themes resolved the bg to n/a while still printing PASS.

pairings.label: Inverse label on inverse fill
pairings.note: The inverse block — a dark strip on a light page, a light strip on a dark page (Chip --primary, Button --inverse; BDS publishes this pair as safe for both tone families in content-system/atmospheres/index.ts:154,168). Second instance of the #1571 shape: the dark brand theme pinned --bds-background-inverse to -black, the same value --bds-text-inverse already held, so the label painted in its own fill at 1.00:1 while ENABLED. Gated AA (4.5:1) not AA-large — an inverse block carries body copy, not just a control label (#1686).

pairings.label: Faded fill-less control label
pairings.note: ADR-028 pt-2: a control with no fill of its own (inputs, checkboxes, radios, switches, ghost/outline labels, menu items) fades on --bds-state-disabled-opacity. `alpha` is the mechanism this dataset lacked until #1687 — opacity composites the label AND the fill toward the same backdrop, producing a pair of computed colours that appear in no token file, so the 26-component fade cohort was unmeasured by construction. This pairing is what pins the token's value: 3.32:1 light / 4.82:1 dark at 0.5, and 2.88:1 light at 0.45. Reading the token name rather than a literal means a retune re-scores here automatically. There is deliberately NO --bds-text-muted counterpart: it is only 3.04:1 against the dark page while ENABLED, so no alpha up to 0.80 rescues it faded (2.30:1 peak), which is why ADR-028 pt-4's muted-text swap was retired rather than retuned (#1687). `scripts/measure-disabled-contrast.mjs` keeps those numbers visible as a report; a pairing here would assert BDS paints it, and nothing does.

pairings.label: Faded SegmentedControl segment label on track

darkException.reason: 3.21:1 light passes; dark is 2.66:1 at 0.5. Only the ITEM carries :disabled — the track never does — and the item is background-color: transparent (SegmentedControl.css:42), so it is correctly on ADR-028 pt-2's fade and `over` points at the track it fades toward rather than the page. That makes this a FOREGROUND problem, not a mechanism one: the label is --bds-text-on-color-light (black) and the dark track is a mid-grey #828282, so fading black toward it collapses the ratio while the enabled pair is a healthy 5.46:1. It is the 'fade plus a foreground that is not the enabled one' class ADR-028 § Consequences pt-2 names. Converting it to the pt-1 swap would repaint a track that nothing disables. Surfaced by #1701; it was invisible before only because no pairing named it.

pairings.label: Brand text on page
pairings.note: Brand-primary text is vibrant poppy-light (brand-kit canon) in its heading/accent role — 3.78:1 on white, gated AA-large (3:1). Small body copy uses --bds-text-primary; usage rule tracked in BDS-18 (BDS-22).

pairings.label: Rail TOC active label on surface
pairings.note: TableOfContents variant="rail" active label — 14px bold, so WCAG large text (18.66px bold) does not apply and the bar is AA 4.5:1, not the AA-large 3:1 that --bds-text-brand-primary carries in its heading/accent role. The rail is now transparent (col_toc dropped its tint, brikdesigns#1458), so the label renders on the band (--bds-surface-primary), not the old --bds-surface-secondary box. --bds-text-brand-primary (poppy-500) is too light; --bds-text-brand-primary-strong darkens to poppy-700 in light and stays poppy-500 in dark, where darkening would sink it (#2270, #2470).

pairings.label: Rail TOC resting label on surface
pairings.note: TableOfContents variant="rail" resting label on the transparent rail's band (--bds-surface-primary). Figma specs --bds-text-muted (#828282) here, which fails AA at label-sm; --bds-text-secondary is the resting label the variant ships (#2270, #2470).

pairings.label: On-color label on brand fill
pairings.note: White CTA label on the vibrant poppy-light brand fill (3.78:1) — a UI-component fill with a large/bold label, gated AA-large (3:1), same basis as the service inverse-card fills (BDS-22).

pairings.label: On-color content block on brand band
pairings.note: ContentBlock --on-color (and SectionHeader forwarding it) on a filled brand band — the CTA-band shape. 3.78:1 in BOTH modes: --bds-surface-brand-primary is --bds-color-poppy-500 under .theme-brand-brik in light AND dark, so this is mode-invariant, unlike the hover/pressed steps below. The surface-side twin of the --bds-background-brand-primary label pairing above, added when the block got its inverse story (#1859) so the pair is measured where the block actually renders. Gated AA-large (3:1), NOT AA, and this one carries BODY COPY (the description slot), not just a large/bold label — the exception the policy's brand-fill clause covers and the 'inverse block carries body copy' reasoning (#1686) does not override, because raising it means darkening the brand fill itself (BDS-22 / ADR-015), not repainting the text. Consumers: keep a band description SHORT; long body copy belongs on a neutral surface. On the brand fill the on-color text is ALWAYS white (--bds-text-on-color-dark) at normal weight: darkening it to --bds-text-primary, or bolding body copy to reach WCAG large-text, are BOTH DISALLOWED — too dark / too heavy for the brand (operator decision 2026-09-12, ADR-015 amendment). Banner --tone-announcement (Banner.css:67-69) already ships this pair.

pairings.label: On-color label on brand fill (hover)
pairings.note: White label on the darkened hover fill (poppy-dark, ~6.2:1 both modes). Fills darken on interaction in light AND dark mode so the white label stays legible; dark mode formerly brightened to poppy-lighter and failed at 1.89:1. --bds-surface-brand-primary-hover resolves to the same value (#1055).

pairings.label: On-color label on brand fill (pressed)
pairings.note: White label on the darkened pressed fill (poppy-darker, ~10.2:1 both modes); dark mode formerly brightened to poppy-lightest and failed at 1.12:1. --bds-surface-brand-primary-pressed resolves to the same value (#1055).

pairings.note: Vibrant brand label on the neutral hover fill (3.38:1 light) — large/semibold button label, gated AA-large (3:1) (BDS-22).

pairings.note: Was ungated (#2096): --bds-text-negative resolved to --bds-color-system-red #eb5757 = 3.48:1 on white. The primitive is darkened to #e52424 (4.56:1 light on white, 4.61:1 dark on black). One theme-invariant value cannot do more: it must sit between L 0.175 (4.5:1 on black) and L 0.183 (4.5:1 on white), so this is the only band that clears both themes.

Solid positive Badge label on fill
pairings.note: Dark badge label on the saturated success fill (6.00:1 both modes). White label was 2.87:1 and failed AA (#995); the fill is light enough that dark text is the accessible pairing.

pairings.label: Rating stars (outlined Testimonial/CardTestimonial) on surface
pairings.note: Stars are a meaningful non-text graphic (role="img" + aria-label), so WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1, not 4.5:1. They used --bds-text-warning (#f2c94c) = 1.59:1 on white (#2697). Pinned to the static primitive --bds-color-yellow-800 (#8e7729): 4.36:1 light, ~3.9:1 dark. The brand variant uses --bds-text-on-color-dark on --bds-surface-brand-primary (existing row above). --bds-text-warning is left unchanged: it feeds fills that pass.

pairings.label: Solid error label on fill
pairings.note: White label on the error fill, 4.56:1 both modes, after --bds-color-system-red was darkened to #e52424 (#2096). Badge solid+negative, Counter, Button and Dialog render this pair. Before the darken the dark label was the passing one (4.95:1; white 3.48:1, #995); it now measures 3.78:1.

pairings.label: Body text on the yellow accent tint
pairings.note: The five accent-{hue} tints are the pale system steps (--color-system-{hue}-light), so a dark label is the accessible pairing in BOTH themes. fg MUST be --bds-text-on-color-light, not --bds-text-primary: --bds-text-primary flips to near-white in dark and measures 1.1–1.2:1 on these tints — the same swap-by-theme trap #1017 records for the inverse hero. Added with #2066, which re-pointed --surface-accent-{hue} off the Brand Kit mid-tone ramp (--color-{hue}-light, itself the deprecated -500 alias from #1739) onto the system tints that surface-positive/negative/warning already use; that lifted purple 5.68 -> 12.87 and orange 5.05 -> 12.80 against dark ink. These five rows are what stop a future re-point back onto a mid-tone ramp.

Label on the red accent fill
pairings.note: The odd one out, and gated AA rather than AAA for that reason. The other five accent surfaces are pale system tints; red has no system tint in canon — the Figma Brand Kit aliases every accent-red purpose to the brand poppy (color/poppy/light [base], #e35335), so --bds-surface-accent-red is a saturated FILL, not a wash (#2066). Dark ink clears 4.56:1 on it, which is AA for a label but short of the AAA body aim the tints hold. Do not put small body copy on this one; Avatar's red initials fill is the shipped consumer (Avatar.css:30) and it pairs --bds-text-on-color-light.

pairings.label: GHL form field border on form background
pairings.note: WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 3:1. The canon GhlForm field border (docs/ghl-form-a11y.css) is --bds-border-input; GHL's own default is #d0d5dd at 1.47:1. A client may override the value, and the override must still clear this floor.

pairings.label: GHL form focus ring on form background
pairings.note: WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.7, 3:1. The canon GhlForm focus ring (docs/ghl-form-a11y.css) is --bds-border-focus. A client may override the value, and the override must still clear this floor.

pairings.label: GHL form checked-checkbox fill on form background
pairings.note: WCAG 1.4.11, 3:1. The canon GhlForm checked fill (docs/ghl-form-a11y.css) is --bds-background-brand-primary. A theme whose brand-primary is dark on a dark form (Birdwell: black on #000000, 1:1) must paste a visible value, and that value must still clear this floor.

pairings.label: Subtle indicator label on the neutral pale fill
pairings.note: The `subtle` appearance of Badge, Tag and Avatar (brik-bds#2943). Each --bds-background-{role}-light holds a pale value in BOTH themes, so the label is the theme-stable dark ink --bds-text-on-color-light, never a theme-flipping --bds-text-{role} (OPERATOR CHOSE 2026-11-03). Gated AA, the indicator-label floor; these eleven rows are what stop a future re-point of a -light fill onto a mid-tone step.
